questions.q: M and R be the mass and radius of a disc. A small disc of radius $R / 3$ is removed from the bigger disc as shown in figure. The moment of inertia of remaining part of bigger disc about an axis AB passing through the centre O and perpendicular to the plane of disc is $\frac{4}{x} M R^2$. The value of $x$ is ________.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Without cavity $\mathrm{I}_1=\frac{\mathrm{MR}^2}{2}$
$\begin{aligned}
\text { Mass of removed disc }= & \frac{\mathrm{M}}{\pi \mathrm{R}^2} \times\left(\frac{\mathrm{R}}{3}\right)^2 \pi \\ & =\left(\frac{\mathrm{M}}{9}\right)
\end{aligned}$
M.I. of removed disc $I_2=\frac{\frac{M}{9}\left(\frac{R}{3}\right)^2}{2}+\frac{M}{9} \times\left(\frac{2 R}{3}\right)^2$
$\begin{aligned}
& =\frac{\mathrm{MR}^2}{18} \\ & \mathrm{I}=\mathrm{I}_1-\mathrm{I}_2=\frac{\mathrm{MR}^2}{2}-\frac{\mathrm{MR}^2}{18}=\frac{4 \mathrm{MR}^2}{9} \\ & (\mathrm{n}=9)
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A thin uniform rod of length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>, cross sectional area <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> and density <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>d</mi></math> is rotated about an axis passing through the centre and perpendicular to its length with angular velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>ω</mi></math>. If value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>ω</mi></math> in terms of its rotational kinetic energy <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>E</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msqrt><mfrac><mrow><mi>α</mi><mi>E</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>d</mi></mrow></mfrac></msqrt></math>, then the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi></math> is ______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Rotational kinetic energy is given by E=12Iω2, here, I is moment of inertia of rod about an axis through its centre and perpendicular to it.

So, E=12ml212ω2

⇒E=12dAl312ω2    ∵mass=density×volume

⇒E=dA(2)324ω2

⇒ω=3EdA

Thus, the value of α=3.

questions.q: If the radius of earth is reduced to three-fourth of its present value without change in its mass then value of duration of the day of earth will be ______ hours 30 minutes.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
By conservation of angular momentum
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{I}_1 \omega_1=\mathrm{I}_2 \omega_2 \\
& \left(\frac{2}{5} \mathrm{MR}^2\right) \frac{2 \pi}{\mathrm{T}_1}=\frac{2}{5} \mathrm{M}\left(\frac{3}{4} \mathrm{R}\right)^2 \frac{2 \pi}{\mathrm{T}_2} \\
& \frac{1}{\mathrm{~T}_1}=\frac{9}{16 \mathrm{~T}_2} \\
& \frac{1}{\mathrm{~T}_2}=\frac{9}{16} \times \mathrm{T}_1=\frac{9}{16} \times 24 \mathrm{hr}=\frac{27}{2} \mathrm{hr}=13 \mathrm{hr} 30 \mathrm{mins} .
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A circular disc reaches from top to bottom of an inclined plane of length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>L</mi><mo>.</mo></math> When it slips down the plane, it takes time <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math>. When it rolls down the plane, it takes time <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mfrac></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msqrt><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi></mfrac></msqrt></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
If disk slips on inclined plane, then its acceleration, a1=gsinθ
L=12a1t12
⇒t1=2 La1 …i

If disk rolls on inclined plane, its acceleration,
a2=gsinθ1+ImR2
a2=gsinθ1+mR22 mR2
a2=23gsinθ
Now L=12a2·t22
⇒t2=2 La2 …ii

Now, t2t1=a1a2=32
⇒x=2

questions.q: Consider a uniform cubical box of side a on a rough floor that is to be moved by applying minimum possible force F at a point b above its centre of mass (see figure). If the coefficient of friction is μ=0.4 , the maximum possible value of 100×ba for a box not to topple before moving is ________
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For no toppling
Fa2+b≤mga2
μa2+μb≤a2
0.2a+0.4b≤0.5a
0.4b≤0.3a
b≤3a2
b≤0.75a (in limiting case)
But it is not possible as b can maximum be equal to 0.5a
∴100bamax=50.00

questions.q: The moment of inertia of a uniform thin rod about a perpendicular axis passing through one end is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>I</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math>. The same rod is bent into a ring and its moment of inertia about a diameter is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>I</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math>. If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><msub><mi>I</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><msub><mi>I</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mfrac></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi><msup><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac></math>, then the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> will be ______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Moment of inertia of rod rotating about an axis passing through one end is I1=ml23     ⋯1 

Moment of inertia of ring rotating about one of its diameters is I2=mR22.

Since the rod is bent into a ring, the circumference of the ring and the length of the rod are equal, l=2πR

Then, I2=mR22=ml28π2 

Thus, the ratio I1I2=8π23, so x=8.

questions.q: A pulley of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> is rotated about its axis by a force <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>F</mi><mo>=</mo><mfenced><mrow><mn>12</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfenced><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></math> applied tangentially (while <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi></math> is measured in seconds). If moment of inertia of the pulley about its axis of rotation is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></math>, the number of rotations made by the pulley before its direction of motion is reversed, will be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>K</mi><mi>π</mi></mfrac></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>K</mi></math> is _____ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Torque of pulley about its axis is τ=Iα, where, I is moment of inertia and α is angular acceleration.

Torque of a force about its axis is τ=FR, here, R is radius of pulley.

Then, 12t-3t21.5=4.5α 

⇒α=4t-t2 

Angular acceleration in terms of angular velocity is

 ⇒α=dωdt=4t-t2

⇒ω=∫0t4t-t2dt

⇒ω=2t2-t33

For ω=0, 2t2-t33=0⇒t22-t3=0

 ⇒t=0 or 6 s

Now, using ω=dθdt, we have

dθdt=2t2-t33⇒θ=∫062t2-t33dt

=2t33-t41206 

=6323-612=638-612=636=36

Number of revolutions =362π=18π

∴K=18

questions.q: A thin rod of mass 0.9 kg and length 1 m is suspended, at rest, from one end so that it can freely oscillate in the vertical plane. A particle of move 0.1 kg moving in a straight line with velocity 80 m s-1 hits the rod at its bottom most point and sticks to it (see figure). The angular speed (in rad s-1) of the rod immediately after the collision will be …………
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given,

Mass of the rod, M=0.9 kg

Mass of particle, m=0.1 kg

Length of the rod, l=1 m

Velocity of particle, v=80 m s-1

No external torque acting on the system of rod and particle, so angular momentum of system about the suspension is conserved, i.e.; Li=Lf

⇒mvl=Iω  ...(1)

Where, I is the momentum of inertia of rod and particle system, ω is the angular velocity of system just after the collision.

⇒mvl=Ml23+ml2ω  ...(2)

Substitute the values in equation (2)

⇒0.1×80×1=0.9×(1)23+0.1×(1)2×ω

ω=20 rad s-1

questions.q: A solid sphere of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> rolls without slipping on a plane surface. Its kinetic energy is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>7</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi></math>. The speed of the centre of mass of the sphere is ______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>cm</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let velocity of centre of mass of sphere be v.

Total kinetic energy of solid sphere is KE=12mv2+12Iω2, where, I is moment of inertia of the solid sphere about the axis passing through it's centre of mass and ω=vR pure rolling condition.

Therefore,

 7×10-3=12×1×(v)2+1225(1)R2vR2

⇒12v275=7×10-3

⇒v2=10-2

⇒v=10-1=0.1 m s-1=10 cm s-1

questions.q: Four particles, each of mass 1 kg are placed at four corners of a square of side 2 m. The moment of inertia of the system about an axis perpendicular to its plane and passing through one of its vertex is ______ kg m2.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the moment of inertia of a system of particles about a point can be written as

I=∑i=1nmiri2   ...1

where, mi is the mass of the ith particle situated at a distance ri from the point.

With reference to the above diagram, it can be written that the net moment of inertia of the system of particles is

I=ma2+ma2+m(2a)2=4ma2=4×1 kg×2 m2=16 kg m2

questions.q:
A 2 kg steel rod of length 0.6 m is clamped on a table vertically at its lower end and is free to rotate in the vertical plane. The upper end is pushed so that the rod falls under gravity. Ignoring the friction due to clamping at its lower end, the speed of the free end of the rod when it passes through its lowest position is _______m s-1.
(Take g=10 m s-2 )
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
In the above case the torque due to weight of the rod, here use the concept of translation work done and rotational kinetic energy, 

⇒W=K.E.⇒mgl=12Iω2, now the moment of inertia of the rod when the axis of rotation passes through one end of the rod, I=1×ml23,
⇒mgl=12×ml23ω2
⇒ω=6gl, now use the relation between linear velocity and angular velocity, 
⇒v=lω=3.6g=6 m s-1

questions.q: Consider a disc of mass 5 kg, radius 2 m, rotating with angular velocity of 10 rad s-1 about an axis perpendicular to the plane of rotation. An identical disc is kept gently over the rotating disc along the same axis. The energy dissipated so that both the discs continue to rotate together without slipping is _________J.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Initial angular momentum, Li=Iωi=MR22·ω=100 kg m2 s-1

Initial kinetic energy, Ei=12·MR22·ω2=500 J

From conservation of angular momentum, we can write

L→i=L→f⇒100=2Iωf

⇒ωf=5 rad s-1

Ef=2×12·5(2)22·(5)2=250 J

Therefore, required energy loss ΔE=250 J

questions.q:
The moment of inertia of a solid disc rotating along its diameter is 2.5 times higher than the moment of inertia of a ring rotating in similar way. The moment of inertia of a solid sphere which has same radius as the disc and rotating in similar way, is $n$ times higher than the moment of inertia of the given ring. Here, $\mathrm{n}=$ _________.
Consider all the bodies have equal masses.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\mathrm{I}_1=\frac{\mathrm{MR}_1^2}{4}, \mathrm{I}_2=\frac{\mathrm{MR}_2^2}{2}, \mathrm{I}_3=\frac{2 \mathrm{MR}_1^2}{5}$ According to problem $\frac{\mathrm{I}_1}{\mathrm{I}_2}=2.5 \Rightarrow \frac{\frac{\mathrm{MR}_1^2}{4}}{\frac{\mathrm{MR}_2^2}{2}}=\frac{5}{2} \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{R}_1^2}{\mathrm{R}_2^2}=5 \ldots$ Now we are provided with information that $\begin{aligned} & \frac{\mathrm{I}_3}{\mathrm{I}_2}=\mathrm{n} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{\frac{2 \mathrm{MR}_1^2}{5}}{\frac{\mathrm{MR}_2^2}{2}}=\mathrm{n} \Rightarrow \frac{4 \mathrm{R}_1^2}{5 \mathrm{R}_2^2}=\mathrm{n} \end{aligned}$ From Eq', (1) and (2) $\Rightarrow n=4$

questions.q: A person of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>80</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> mass is standing on the rim of a circular platform of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>200</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> rotating about its axis at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn></math> revolutions per minute (rpm). The person now starts moving towards the centre of the platform. What will be the rotational speed (in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>rpm</mi></math> ) of the platform when the person reaches its centre....
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Applying conservation of angular momentum,

mR2+MR22ω=MR22ω'

80+2002×5=2002ω'

ω'=9rev/sec.

questions.q: A circular disc of mass <math><mtext>M</mtext></math> and radius <math><mtext>R</mtext></math> is rotating about its axis with angular speed <math><mrow><msub><mi>ω</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow></math>. If another stationary disc having radius <math><mrow><mfrac><mtext>R</mtext><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></math> and same mass <math><mtext>M</mtext></math> is dropped co-axially on to the rotating disc. Gradually both discs attain constant angular speed <math><mrow><msub><mi>ω</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></math>. The energy lost in the process is <math><mrow><mtext>p%</mtext></mrow></math> of the initial energy. Value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">p</mi></math> is ______
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
I1ω1+I2ω2=I1+I2×ωf

 

MR22×ω+0MR22+MR281625

ωf=45ω

Final K.E., Kf=12MR22+MR281625ω2

Kf=MR2ω25 ; Ki=12MR22ω2=MR2ω24

Percentage loss in kinetic energy % loss=MR2ω24−MR2ω25MR2ω24×100=20%

questions.q: A solid sphere and a solid cylinder of same mass and radius are rolling on a horizontal surface without slipping. The ratio of their radius of gyrations respectively <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><msub><mi>k</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mi>p</mi><mi>h</mi></mrow></msub><mo>:</mo><msub><mi>k</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mi>y</mi><mi>l</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mfenced></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo>:</mo><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is _______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Considering rotational axis as the diametrical axis for sphere and axis of cylinder. Then

K12=25R2 and K22=12R2

∴ K1K2=2/51/2=45

⇒K1K2=25

Comparing it with the given value in the question,

25=2x

questions.q: For rolling spherical shell, the ratio of rotational kinetic energy and total kinetic energy is x5. The value of x is _____.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The rotational kinetic energy is given by 

Krot=Iω22=13MR2ω2.

The total kinetic energy is given by 

Ktot=12mv2+13MR2ω2=mR2ω22+13MR2ω2=56MR2ω2

Thus, the ratio is 

KrotKtot=13MR2ω256MR2ω2=25

Comparing with the given value,

x5=25⇒x=2

questions.q: Four identical discs each of mass 'M' and diameter 'a' are arranged in a small plane as shown in figure. If the moment of inertia of the system about OO' is x4Ma2. Then, the value of x will be _____ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Considering four identical discs as 1, 2, 3 and 4.

Moment of inertia of disc about diagonal is I1=I3=MR24

Now using parallel axis theorem, 

Moment of inertia of disc 2 and 4 is 

I2=I4=MR24+MR2=54MR2

So, net moment of inertia about OO' is 

 I=I1+I2+I3+I4

=2MR24+254MR2

 =MR22+52MR2=3MR2

Putting R=a2

I=3Ma24, so,x=3

We know, θ=ω1+ω22t

Let number of revolutions be N

∴2πN=2π900+246060×2×26

N=728
